notes.title: Incoming Patch for All Corrosive Studios RPGs
notes.content:
Corrosive Supporters!

Hey guys! Instead of making several individual announcement posts, I'm making this one to cover all the bases.

https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/6836576/1a3994ccd145768199bf31edb79d01bdea1cb37d.png

A patch will be released for the following games shortly: Waste Walkers and all of its expansions, Disgraced, Lawless Lands and its expansion, and later on with the next update - Chaos Chain.

The patch is to fix a long standing issue in relation to changing equipment in combat. There was an issue with the code in relation to using the mouse where the FPS would tank when hovering over an equipment slot that currently had something equipped in it. There was a loop that was causing the info panel to CONSTANTLY refresh EVERY frame (60 times a second) and that obviously takes a huge toll on performance.

I never realized how bad it was until I was working today on Chaos Chain. The issue was present in all my previous RPGs but I never even noticed. The only reason I found it now is because Chaos Chain has A LOT of slots for equipment (both actual equipment and then the augmentation slots for cyber/bioware), so the whole screen gets super laggy and it was just awful.

Anyways, it's fixed now. The patch for each game will be live shortly, I am just waiting for the builds to be complete and then I can start uploading.

Thanks for reading and for your support!

-Cryptic ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 8/12/22 - MASSIVE Chaos Chain Update 1.3.5
notes.content:
Chaos Chain

Hey everyone! I wanted to share this here so everyone can check it out if they're interested!

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/2976a984d1680cf0de470596942bda50d3b7983b.jpg

Update 1.3.5 Change Log:

Bug Fixes:

Extended battle background image width by 100 to account of screen shake (It showed black around the edges and looked odd)
Fixed an unreachable container in the Condemned Apartments Second Floor area
Fixed Crescent Strip Metro Station characters not saving their locations
Fixed ranged attacks being counted as Cyber in some cases
Fixed a bug that showed weapons listed in the ammo slot possible equips list but did not allow them to be selected (They should not show up at all in the list now like how it should be - This bug drove me crazy for a very long time)
Fixed a few stat inconsistencies related to equipment
Fixed some tileset shading
Fixed some gaps in certain tileset entities such as tables and countertops
Fixed Smelling Salts text not being colored like other medical items
Fixed some dialogue texts running off screen
Got rid of duplicate models/objects in several tilesets
Fixed an issue which prevented ANY critical hits from happening in certain cases
Fixed criticals not multiplying properly in certain cases (If the original damage of an attack was 0 but the random roll was applied - It was happening after the fact)
Fixed Hunker Down skill not properly reducing extra damage rolls (Hunker Down should be A LOT more useful now)
Fixed inconsistent damage rate issues
Fixed Blinded status temporarily removing control of the character (Not intended)
Fixed some runoff text with some quest descriptions in the menu
Fixed optimize equipment not optimizing certain slots if they relied on stats from other slots (Example: Neural Link grants ability to equip hackpads but since headgear is below the gadget slot, it could never optimize hackpads)
Fixed Ammo slot not optimizing ever (It might not always be perfect because different bonuses are based on player preference instead of what is "better" for ammo types
Fixed some minor typos
Fixed a PDA color code inconsistency
Fixed some status effect priorities for sorting status effects listed on characters in combat


Changes & Additions:

Added some new Steam achievements
Old saves will now automatically fetch quest data from the current set up to update automatically to the latest version (This means old saves won't get stuck with old data for quests anymore)
Added Industrial Zone new city district area! (The gameplay area just grew by about 20% - This area is also one of the largest yet!)

notes.title: 6/22/22 GIANT Chaos Chain Update 1.2.8
notes.content:
Chaos Chain

Salutations, dwellers...

Here is the next GIANT update for the game, as promised. There are a TON of changes in this update, so it is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to start a new game if you have an old save. They will likely still work just fine, but there will be inconsistencies and may be problems.

Let's discuss some of the highlights.

First, you can now go directly to the Steam update news for the game from the main menu. You can also see the new greenish coloring of the selection box here.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/6f885301ba5309e698619d260386de14499e4782.png

Next, the resistances page has been better organized by side, and you can also see that electronic damage is now called interference. This is because the FIRST VERSION OF THE COMBAT HACKING SYSTEM IS NOW IN GAME.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/9601d03d4f74098e12b8e24a4361e92699588aac.png

A preview of the first two combat hacks. Bypass and Exploit.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/40a528e78eb072cda62b60af247e202df93cd1d2.png

The techie now begins the game with a hackpad (pretty much a cyberdeck) as seen here.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/5cb5904f3271fecb75a107e3489a686a580ca874.png

Next, the PDA now tells you what soundtrack is currently playing and has a shuffle option in the overview submenu. Lots of new soundtracks have been added.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/7e4fecd7a19110ceb37cacc5ae26f3ecaf8b8ed4.png

Another major change to show off is two handed weapons and heavy weapons now have a "Heavy" trait which makes them require two hands. Making it so you cannot use a gadget at the same time. This does mean that for melee weapons with Heavy, they get some benefits as described in the change log below.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/99452c948f3635ed329318b8e563748d14c1c57a.png

Beyond that, there are an absolute TON OF OTHER CHANGES, ADDITIONS, AND IMPROVEMENTS.

Check out the change log below!

Please note that these changes are not in any particular order.

Update 1.2.8 Change Log:

Bug Fixes:

Fixed a bug where companions could still be removed from the party if they were dead/broken but healed/recovered
Fixed Bull still being present outside The Eclipse after completing "Head in the Clouds P2" (Saves that are at this point won't automatically make him leave, but it isn't a huge deal - You don't really have to see him leave, it's just inferred he's doing investigating on his end too - This wasn't really a bug but more of something I wanted to add)
Fixed world modifiers array displaying some of them in the middle of the screen and some at the bottom
Fixed Anti Toxins spawning so frequently in loot containers (Moved them to the random drug/medicine list)
Fixed dialogue with Tara where you offer to help her showing  Tanya's face graphic momentarily
Fixed Flak conversation not having a loop to the top after you buy equipment from him, which resulted in floating labels getting stuck off and forcing you to re-enable it
Fixed an unintentional setting in the "Shady Dealings" side quest where the quest related area (No spoilers) was still able to be entered after the quest was completed (Old saves will still be able to go in there one last time before it automatically closes, but it's not a big deal - This was just an oversight)
Fixed battlebackgrounds not having any battle motion (They are supposed to shift ever so subtly)
Fixed tilesets with metal fences (Chain link) not being evenly aligned properly with their vertical bars
Fixed enemies not using their full array of combat skills if their dedicated attack skill had too high of a priority (This was a bug that I did not realize existed until now, but was introduced in the update where I made regular attacks much more frequent... too frequent - I ran 30 rounds of combat and watched 5 enemies just repeatedly do their standard attack on my guy as I kept dev healing - that's 150 attack actions and no other actions chosen - After the fix, they immediately started using other skills instead)
Added a failsafe to protect against a rare crash when picking world modifiers in an old save in specific circumstances
Fixed [spoiler]Grady[/spoiler] boss having some extra stat benefits that he wasn't meant to have (Extra evasion and initiative)
Trip and Lights Out abilities no longer adds your weapon stats to the attack
Heads up balloons are now closer to the character they originate from and better centered
Fixed a bug with the randomized protestor dialogue playing a line twice in one case
Fixed a bug with the confused status effect not lasting the correct amount of turns
Added a failsafe to prevent incorrect damage calculations in certain circumstances


Changes & Additions:

Added some new Steam Achievements
Finished "Relief Recovery" side quest (This quest has several different outcomes and several different ways to complete it)
Added an "Update News" option to the main title menu (Opens the Chaos Chain update feed on Steam)
Added a set bool to off command to the beginning of the cyware/biware check functions (For determining what kind - if any - of augments the player character has implanted - this will help the game more efficiently keep track of player character status and avoid any unwanted situations relating to the system)
Enemies are MUCH more likely to retreat now at either critical health or critical mettle (Morale)
Reduced animation size of the enemy retreat skill
Electronic damage renamed to Interference damage
Updated item/equipment descriptions for the change above this one
All characters by default (With no Cyberware) are 100% immune to the Glitched Status Effect (I had to do some reworking of the existing system, so old characters likely won't auto-update to this new setting)
All characters by default (With no Cyberware) are 100% immune to the Interference Damage (From hacking/cyber attacks - I had to do some reworking of the existing system, so old characters likely won't auto-update to this new setting)
Tasers, Stun Guns, and Shock Batons now do base (Default) damage instead of interference (This was an oversight when I implemented the cyberware system for how the damage was going to be calculated) but their damage formula has been reduced to account for this change
Added the very first version of the Hack Pad system (Basically cyberdecks to avoid any confusion - They require a processor implanted to be usable)
Added Ice Breaker Hack Pad (Gives Bypass and Exploit cyber attacks - First one is used to status effect the enemy and cripple them, second one is to crush them - THERE ARE NOT MANY ENEMIES TO USE THESE ON YET - THIS IS ONLY THE FIRST STEP TOWARDS GETTING THE SYSTEM IMPLEMENTED)
Glitched status effect now increases damage taken through interference damage by 20%
Added Bypass cyber skill and animation (3-9 Interference Damage, +70% Glitched, +10 Initiative On Use)
Added Exploit cyber skill and animation (7-13 Interference Damage, +5 Initiative On Use, +5% Glitched)
Techie character background now starts with the Ice Breaker Hack Pad instead of the infovisor
Processors now allow use of hack pads, hack pads now allow use of cyber skills
Updated Glitched status effect animation
Enemies will now use their full array of combat skills (As long as necessary conditions are met such as low health for bandaging, etc)
Added some new randomized main character names to the list (We're over 270 now)
Increased player-message interaction sound cues by 5%
All Plot related items are now marked with a "*" before their name so they are immediately recognizable
Version info will now only display on the main (title screen) menu and the in game menu interface
Choice selection color is now a faint green instead of the pink/red and the outline box has been updated to be more clear
Slightly increased all window background opacities
Updated difficulty selection tooltip to explain world modifiers
Default character name is no longer blank so you're forced to either enter a name or randomize it (The default names are the old Victor/Victoria, but you can still enter your own or randomly generate one - This is just so it doesn't start off completely blank in the box)
Adjusted EXP rewards on some side quests
Updated the journal description for "Head in the Clouds P3"
Added a new hint for the "Relief Recovery" side quest
Added Condemned Apartments: Basement area
Added Condemned Apartments: Storage area
Added new battle background graphic"Grungeinterior2"
Slightly reduced delay between randomized sound effects playing
Added helicopter flyby sound effect to the randomized sound effects lists
Added 5 more glass breaking sound effects to the randomized sound effects lists
Added 2 more wood breaking sound effects to the randomized sound effects lists
Added randomized earthquakes to the randomized sound effects list (It's a slight screen shake and sound - very rare, just for extra atmosphere)
Added randomized blackouts to the randomized sound effects list (The screen will fade to very dark and play a sound for a moment, then recover the screen and play another sound - very rare, just for extra atmosphere)
Damage values are now rounded to the NEAREST integer instead of the integer in which they are a part of (3.6 will turn into 4 instead of 3, 2.2 will turn into 2)
Added proper immunity checking to certain damage type handling to account for the extra random damage roll added onto all damage (If immune to a damage type, no extra damage will be added and the attack will fail - Example: Cyber attacks against a sewer rat probly won't do much..........)
EMP Grenades now deal interference damage as they should have originally but I was waiting for me to get some of the hacking system work done
Added some new character graphics
Added several new enemy graphics (Sprites and battlers)
Added thug slicer enemy
Added thug shooter enemy
Added thug vandal enemy
Added thug punk enemy
Added some new enemy groups
Added new bandit/thug boss (No spoilers - He is heavily cybered though and a perfect target for the new hackpad system)
Enemy pain/hurt sounds are now set to 80% volume instead of 100% because many of them are pretty loud
The resistances panel in the character record now lists all element resistances on one side and state resistances on the other to be more uniform (They were mixed previously)
Both cyber-based resistances (Glitched Resistance and Interference Resistance) are now listed at the bottom of the resistances panel to be easier to find and side-by-side to be more obvious that they go together
Further tweaks to the interface color/contrast settings to make it easier to read
Added some new special NPCs to interact with and talk to
Added multiple new generic NPCs to several areas
Added NPC blockers to a few areas to prevent them from getting in the way
Shields now count as armor but still equip just as before (Everything will still work the same way, this is just to help with easier classification)
Targeting Assisted Bracers now equip to the support slot and count as gear instead of a gadget
All Long Guns now prevent use of a gadget at the same time (Two handed)
Some Small Guns now prevent use of a gadget at the same time (Two handed - Examples are shotguns and sub-machine guns)
All Ordinance Weapons (Grenade launchers, rocket launchers, machine guns, etc) now prevent use of a gadget at the same time (Two handed)
Categorized Melee Weapons based on how they may be used (Some of them will now prevent using a gadget at the same time due to being Two Handed - Examples: Sledge Hammer, Fire Axe)
Added "2H" to all descriptions of weapons that require two hands
All heavy (Two handed) melee and exotic weapons now give a new status effect on their target to make them more impactful given that they cannot be used with gadgets (Shaken - this lasts for 1 turn and gives: -2% to hit, -2% critical chance, -3% mettle, -3 initaitive)
Added "Heavy" to all melee and exotic weapons that require two hands and give the "Shaken" status
Updated enemies using heavy melee weapons with the above status application
Added some rust spots to trash cans to give them more detail
Updated some of the graphics for trash and clutter with more detail
Added a few more loot containers spread around some areas
Added some more clutter to a few areas
Slightly reduced overall chance of loot spawning in containers
Slightly increased chance of ammo spawning in containers
Added "Stranger" title for everyone
Added "Chromed" title for anyone who gets cyberware installed (For old saves, you'll have to wait until you get more cyberware)
Added "Altered" title for anyone who gets bioware installed (For old saves, you'll have to wait until you get more bioware)
Added enemy abilities to use drugs in combat to give them an edge (Usage is rare)
Added enemy "Grace" drug skill
Added enemy "Twitch" drug skill
Added enemy "Voodoo" drug skill
Added enemy "Zeal" drug skill
Added drugs (Grace, Twitch, Voodoo, Zeal) to enemy drop lists
Enemy gutter rats now have a very small chance to drop rotten food, rags, and bobby pins (3%/3%/1%)
Added 15 new battle soundtracks
Added 29 new exploration soundtracks
Added 19 new title screen soundtracks
Added several new gun sound effects (For use later)
Added 5 more random soundtracks to the player apartment
Renamed "Your Apartment Key" to "Your Apt Key"
Updated some item descriptions
Added a song switch in the intro between the world background and the foreword
Soundtracks will now save between maps so that the game does not reselect a new track every time you switch maps (UNLESS THE MAP HAS A SPECIFIC SOUNDTRACK SET - In which case, the music track will change while in that specific map and then go back to the previous track when you leave)
Slightly increased duration of soundtracks playing before switching
Added some new roleplay dialogue options
Added A LOT of new dialogues with various existing characters and new characters
Data Item/Lore Item is now listed as special instead of plot
Added Soundtrack submenu to the Overview menu in the PDA
Added Shuffle Soundtrack option to the PDA Overview -> Soundtrack submenu
Updated fast travel (Metro) background sound effect
Updated the map icon art in the menu (It's a map ping now instead of intersecting metro lines)
Removed specific soundtracks for several general areas (Now, only very specific special areas have set soundtracks - this may make certain areas/situations feel out of place with the currently selected soundtrack from time to time, but I think this way is better - if you feel differently, please explain your feelings on the subject - also, if you find any soundtracks that really seem out of place or feel like they don't fit the cyberpunk vibe enough, please tell me)
Blinker Flash special ability is now listed as an ability instead of a cyber skill
Added 1 more empty row between each line in the intro to allow more reading time
Updated some item icon art
Very slightly reduced the base movement speed
Added some new quest related special events
Rewrote the randomized additional damage on attacks code to make it more efficient
Optimized some systems and processes to be more efficient
Cleaned up more old/unused code
TONS of other minor tweaks, improvements, and changes all throughout the game


NOTE: You DON'T need to start a new game, but it is always recommended. Especially if you encounter any odd issues after a large update.

Please let me know of any bugs or issues you may encounter. The update will be available shortly.

For more info on the game, visit the store page below!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1536730/Chaos_Chain/

That's all for now, enjoy!

Hey everyone!

I hope you're all enjoying the most recent update from last week. Since then, I have been working on adding new areas and coming up with new quests/plots as well as adding new equipment and items!

notes.title: Chaos Chain - 2/13/22 Development Status Update
notes.content:
Chaos Chain

Hey everyone!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/80fa8b5a587249492bc207a72e6d2a968ead30ea.png

I just wanted to take a moment and give you a status update on how development for the game has been going.

So far, the February major content update (the first major content update for the game, in fact) is going well. I'm not as far along as I would have liked, there has been a lot of important matters I needed to focus my attention and time on in my personal life over the past two weeks. It's been quite busy and a little more stressful than I would like, but things are finally starting to settle down.

As far as the content that I've added so far, I have implemented a working, fully-rounded cyberware upgrade system. By my count, there are 35 different cyber upgrades that you can get at the moment. I have many more ideas that will be added as well, but 35 is pretty good to start us off. I also added the very first cyber related skill which comes from one of the optical upgrades called "Blinker Flash". Basically, your cyber optics emit a sudden, bright flash similar to a flashbang, but a little less effective. The ability can blind and even confuse your foes. Many (many, many, many) more abilities are planned, but for now, this is what I've added. I've been focusing on the actual upgrade system first to get everything in place.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39690716/f59f0e83b6b609469d51010aa7fe42417fba2015.png

For new playable areas and content, I have not had the time yet to do much, unfortunately. I have added "The Descent" night club in Ashen Row (metal themed bar) which has a black market cyberware operation going on in the basement - that's where you can get some cyberware for your emerging cyborg. Beyond that, this week (starting tomorrow) will be my time to focus on new playable content as that is most important in my opinion, but the cyberware system was something I at the very least wanted to get established. I also added a few new firearms to try out including the Brunetta Avenger tactical pump shotgun and the Armican Pride heavy pistol.

I've done some more character sprites to continue the trend of nearly all npcs (even generic npcs) being somewhat unique. Thanks to my friend, AceHangman, for doing some more sprite graphics, we now have even more hair and clothing options. There will be more selectable skins and faces in the future for your character as well, but since there are already so many, it's not on my list of priorities at this time.

I am still hoping to get this major content update fully completed and delivered by the end of February, but I am a bit behind. Not only has there been personal matters to attend to, but recently there was a major storm in my area that pretty much closed everything down for two whole days, so instead of working, I was worrying about staying warm and keeping things all taken care of here with my family. I apologize that I'm not further along on this update yet, I really would have liked to be. I may have to move some of my planned additions from this update to the next one due to these events, or I could delay the update a bit, but I'd rather not do it that way. What do you guys think?

Anyways, I'll wrap this up for now. 

Thanks for reading.

notes.title: Chaos Chain - Development Status Update 1/23/22
notes.content:
Chaos Chain,

Hey everyone!

It's been a bit since I've posted a status update for the game, but development has continued as normal.

I'm planning on releasing the game in Early Access this coming week towards the end of the week (Thursday or Friday if all goes according to plan) and I'm excited to hear what everyone thinks.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1536730/Chaos_Chain

I've been working a lot on polishing the game as it is right now, bug testing/fixing, and adding more playable content. I have a handful of side quests, lots of equipment and gear, a custom gambling minigame, lots of lore, highly detailed environments, and the beginning to the main story all just about ready to go, but I need a few more days to finalize everything for the first release. I wanted to answer some potential questions for people below so they can learn more about what the game has to offer.

Q&A

Some things to be aware of for the game's initial release:
1 - The game is NOT all about combat. Roleplaying, dialogues, branching situations/events, and different outcomes are just as important, if not more so. Combat in the game is DIFFICULT but FAIR.
2 - The game doesn't have a ton of playable content yet. It is just the beginning of the main story and a handful of side quests and some areas to explore. Everything does work very well right now though and it is a pretty polished experience. I will be adding a TON more content throughout development however, just as I have with my previous projects.
3 - The game will be priced at $7.99 (or your local equivalent) initially with two optional DLC supporter packs ($2.99/$5.99) if you'd like to help me out and support the game's development further. The final price of the game is still to be determined depending on how much I add and how far it goes, but buying in Early Access will get you a discount either way.
4 - I plan to take suggestions and feedback from the community all throughout development like with my previous games. If you have something you'd like to contribute, feel free to post on the forums.
5 - The game does have some mature content/topics so please be aware of that. There is no nudity or racism, but there is harsh language, implied drug use, gambling, references to prostitution and gang/criminal activities, and so on. It is pretty general mature content.
6 - Development will likely go on for about a year depending on how things go. I will be releasing content pretty quickly (especially now that the foundation is done) and plan to release large updates monthly and patches weekly.
7 - The game does have achievements and will hopefully get trading cards, but that is up to the community to help me out with. Trading cards on Steam are locked behind a sales quota (that we don't have any direct answer to as to what the quota is) so it's not guaranteed unless community interest is high enough.
8 - Yes, there is a cyberware/cyboring upgrade system already in place, but it is currently unavailable until I do more testing and do more work on it. Right now, I'm focusing on adding actual gameplay content.
9 - The game world is going to be the entirety of Slade City, a fictional metropolis set in the United States approximately 50 years in the future. Right now, there are two districts to explore, but there will likely be at least 10 (plus all the interior areas inside them) as well as extra areas for missions and so on.
10 - Just ask if there is anything else you'd like to know.

Thanks for reading!

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Chaos Chain Dev Update 9/3/21
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I'm back with another quick status update. I wanted to go over another QOL feature I created today.

In the past with my games, I have always had some non-important NPCs with generic greetings. These could be common people, guards, and even some enemies. Their messages could contain useful information or lore, but they were mainly just there to populate the game world and simulate an inhabited location such as a village or hideout.

The issue I had with the system was that their dialogue was not important, but still appeared as a regular message and even if they only had a few words to say, it would take a good moment to read and then you'd have to click again on them to make the message go away. Not a huge deal, but since it's not anything important, it could be annoying and feel repetitive.

So, I created a system that I call "SpeakUp". It's very simple and it's just an addition to a system I already had in place, but it makes the game flow better in my opinion.

Speak Up
https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/973622e22d781d2b5a98256218c304fe5dc67f5f.png

In the above screenshot, I am just talking to a generic NPC Junkie who apparently doesn't like the look of my character. He doesn't have any vital information, but some of his randomized lines may prove to have lore, information, or hints about the game world just like in my previous projects.

Some of you will find this familiar if you've played my last game, Lawless Lands. In that game, whenever you got a reputation change, experience, traveled, or when the weather changed, a message would appear similarly to let you know what happened.

Now, when you're talking to an NPC who isn't plot-related, their message will appear on the screen for a moment and they'll show a chat bubble over their head to let you know they're speaking to you. A faint sound will also play.

Anyways, that's all for now. I hope to get more done next week - I have been sick this week so didn't have much energy to tackle anything too big.

I'll have more info soon!

Thank you for reading!

notes.title: Chaos Chain - Equipment Briefing
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

For those of you who missed the last announcement discussing my next project, Chaos Chain, you can find that here to get you up to date: 

https://steamcommunity.com/groups/CorrosiveStudios/announcements/detail/5246117291297561777

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/37cf25db4ec95381cb2716184fc089383d55739f.jpg

For those of you who already know of the new game, let's talk about equipment.

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/64df151097805d3f020cf38222ae5ff5ab46baa3.png

Equipment has always played a significant role in my past games. Having the right tools for the job at hand is extremely important in my opinion, so I try to put that into the game worlds.

For Chaos Chain, this will still apply, but the system has been expanded and improved from my other projects.

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/e79ae69e93dd2b97e560bd4ca9c4d5fd258f6772.png

First, as you can hopefully see in the image above, weapons have a pretty significant stat-line. A lot is taken into account and much thought went into how the stats function and what ratings each weapon was given. It may look simplistic, but each specific stat has a lot of factors to think about such as handling, ease of use, accuracy, speed, range, capabilities of fire modes such as semi, burst, and auto. The engine is somewhat limited, but I have done my best so far (still a lot of room for improvement) to make weapons feel unique.

Second, I've done A LOT of work on improving the combat system. I can't really show it off here right now, but something I'd like to mention is an EXTREME focus on sound effects and quick-flow combat. Weapons have unique sound effects and animations so you can tell what you are using compared to your enemies. I have improved the default battle sound system to include a variety of sound effects for each event so it's not always the same exact boring sound. There are several sound effects for each event like for example an evasion/dodge has multiple sounds of its own and then there are special sounds for bullets missing or a melee weapon hitting someone. I personally think that sounds make or break a game - especially when you're hearing the same ones over... and over... and over.

So far, I have around 50 or so weapons which are mostly melee weapons and improvised weapons, but I have a handful of fictional (based on real) firearms across a variety of different archtypes including pistols, PDWs (personal defense weapons), SMGs (submachine guns), shotguns, assault rifles, battle rifles, carbines, sniper rifles, machine guns, rocket launchers, grenade launchers, special weapons, and even some exotic weaponry. Not all of these are ready yet, but that's the weapon archtype/class lineup I'm going for. Like in my first game, Waste Walkers, firearms will allow for different ammunition types such as full metal jacket, hollow point, armor piercing, buckshot, slugshot, and birdshot, and even more are planned to be added. Depending on your preference, the different ammunitions will provide different bonuses.

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/dc388ee7d346efb58f2c76172103a2de5ecb95a9.png

Armor is the same way - they have a lot to take into account. One flaw of my previous games in my opinion is that armor resistances were very minor. A 5% here, maybe a lucky 15% there, etc. The idea was to stack up on resistances you favored with your combination of chosen gear. Most of the time, the numbers didn't add up enough to actually make any significant impact. That will NOT be the case here. The equipment slot system is more straight forward, but each slot has a specific purpose. Armor is armor. It should feel like it. In the above picture, you can see the current (subject to change) stats for the ballistic vest. The resistance percentages are high enough by themselves to actually protect you from different damage types, but they may be bolstered even more by accompanying gear in other slots such as the head slot for headgear or even the accessory slot.

Theoretically speaking, if your punk has 8 health remaining and an enemy thug stabs you with a shiv for 10 puncture damage (lucky roll) and you have a protection (armor) value of 2, a toughness of 4, and a 25% puncture resistance, you'll only take 3 damage. The detailed math: 10 damage - (2 protection - 4 toughness) * .75 = 3. That's pretty helpful. Taking a third of the dealt damage because of having decent armor instead of the full amount just kept you alive. A leather jacket (armor 1 with a puncture protection of 5%) would have left you dead in the street. The differences between armor types should no longer feel minimal.

That's all for now, I'll have more information soon!

Thanks for reading!

-Eric "Corrosion" Plasencia

notes.title: What's Next from Corrosive Studios? "Chaos Chain"
notes.content:
Hey everyone, Corrosion here.

So, several people have been asking me recently about what I've been working on lately.

I didn't want to give any info out too early, but I think now is a great time for me to tell you all a bit about my new project. 

Let me start by saying that it's very early in development, so nothing you see is finalized.

Chaos Chain
A dark cyberpunk roleplaying game by Corrosive Studios

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/37cf25db4ec95381cb2716184fc089383d55739f.jpg

-This is a project that I have been working on for a few months and it's finally starting to actually take form. The game is heavily inspired by a variety of movies and games including The Matrix, Johnny Mnemonic, Shadowrun, The Terminator, Total Recall, Repo Men, Cyberpunk 2021 (RPG), and a whole lot more. Of course, I'm only trying to get inspiration for the genre, so Chaos Chain will have a lot of its own content and lore. I'm really passionate about bringing this all to life, so I hope some of you like it so far.

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/ad37bef03793018501f2f1a2c1573b88391c1e1a.gif

Background:
"Half a century into the future, mankind's world is riven and in a state of great social, political, and economic strain... After the end of the horrific pandemic that haunted the early twenties, big pharma became stronger than ever seen before. Medical research thrived and allowed for a multitude of tech advancements, but healthcare prices skyrocketed, causing mass inflation and shifting the world's economy... As a result, cryptocurrencies grew in popularity and eventually gained enough momentum to replace other monetary systems across the globe... Greed, hatred, envy, and panic then fueled the fires of war time after time, leaving the world scarred and broken. The U.N. has fallen and the war on terror has failed. Civilization is slowly collapsing in on itself... Now, most people cannot afford their basic needs. Society is fragmented and has dissolved back into a rigid caste division. Crime is at an all-time high and poverty is the new norm. Each day that passes, exploitation of the Earth's resources continues and pollution intensifies, making life even more unbearable... Humanity is in the darkest place of its entire existence... A dark place where you exist."

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/fecced5e2930fa5078cdd9757356c4f6e914ceb0.jpg

It's still very early off, and it will be a bit before anything is playable, but it's getting there.

-For the game's mechanics, I have read through a lot of reviews and feedback that I've gained over the years. I tried to create a good mix of both complexity and simplicity to make the game straight forward, but also unique, also while being enjoyable. There is no durability, no overly complicated armor systems, damage is straight forward, weapons and classifications for them are easy to understand, and so on.

-I want to create a game with a HEAVY EMPHASIS ON ACTUAL ROLEPLAYING. In the past, I did this with Lawless Lands, but I want it to have even more depth. Branching dialogues, non-linear sequences, player-influenced-events based on choices and character builds, and many other ideas. I want the player's place in the game to have a direct tie in to what they do. For better or for worse. I also want to highlight that the game will not be combat focused. It will still feature combat though. Basically, I just really want the game to be much more dynamic and personalized based on how the player interacts with the game world.

-Combat as it is right now, is quick, painful, and dirty. Even if you have a clear advantage, you're still likely to come out with some scratches on you. Of course, armor will help - and much more effectively than my previous games at that. Weapon capabilities are also more diversified and streamlined, making them more useful depending on the situation. I've already made changes (a lot) to the combat system to make it more enjoyable and dangerous. For you and the enemies. I've also decided to make custom animations for EVERY WEAPON so it may take longer, but I think it'll make it a lot better. 

-The game is not always meant to be perfectly "fair", but that counts for everyone. What I mean is, if you can do something, your enemy likely can to and vice versa, but sometimes you may find yourself in a serious bind and you'll need to play your cards carefully to get yourself out.

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/9183f8dbd6c925d659fee4a7908686336dff2dbf.jpg

-I'm pretty much building it from the ground up from scratch, creating a lot of custom assets (and a friend is helping me with character design stuff) so it will take time, but it will also be much more original. For music (soundtracks), I have a really awesome selection that fits my vision perfectly. I'm really excited to see it all put together.

-For character creation/design, I can say that there is a TON OF DEPTH. Skills, attributes, traits, flaws (something new that I wanted to do), occupation, etc. Characters are not all-powerful. They have limits and drawbacks. Psychological trauma and defects as well as physical with varying effects. Backgrounds will give key bonuses in various areas of influence that can help or hinder you in situations depending on what you have available. There are also going to be more out of combat skills so the game has more variety.

There is a lot more I want to talk about and show off, but this is already turning into a novel, so I will wrap it up for now.

If you want to discuss the game, give ideas, or just have the link to the hub, you can find a link to the Chaos Chain Steam Community Hub here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1536730

I'll have more information soon.

Thanks for reading!

https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6836576/551a162736ad2ccd578f3145ff1e02529870d419.png

-Eric "Corrosion" Plasencia

notes.content:

So, as many of you know, the stealth system was a little lackluster in the game. This is no longer the case.

Another change is the addition of their sight awareness for flashlight detection. If the player has their flashlight on and is within a certain distance, the AI will now react as if they are startled and begin trying to take the player down!

Further changes include extending the backstab range when attempting to sneak up behind an enemy to melee them, the AI now have slightly further distance of detection.

One side change to the AI is the addition of an ammo counter system so enemy characters will now need to reload every so often, too! Adding a whole new level of complexity and randomness to combat!

Numerous other changes to the AI have also been made but those were mainly adjustments and fine tuning.

The Stealth System update will come with the release of chapter 5 - Relapse. Coming soon! This update is going to be HUGE!

That's all for now!

notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey guys!

So, as many of you know, something has always been missing from Affliction. Immersion. The game lacks certain aspects and features that makes for great modern shooters. This should no longer be the case!

So, I posted a status update yesterday in the middle of the day after having worked all morning but then I continued working late into the night on improving the AI.

After a few hours of solid coding, I can safely say that the next update will SIGNIFICANTLY improve the AI in every single way. Flanking, maneuvering, using cover, suppressive fire, constant target acquisition, and many more behaviors have been added for the human AI.

This was a major breakthrough for the game. Truly. This major improvement will come with the release of chapter 4 and all of it's goodies. Coming soon.

notes.title: 12/21/17 Development Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey everyone!

Here's another quick status update to talk about progress being made on the game.

Over the past few days, the next map that takes place directly after the events in chapter 3 in the game has been completed. It came out pretty good and I can't wait to hear what people think. This is a much bigger map than many of the others currently in the game.

I've received a lot of feedback concerning the AI in the game and most of it has said they need to be improved. I agreed completely so another thing that I've been working on is improving it. I can now say that combat will be significantly more dynamic and the AI is much smarter and more realistic. Adding some extra event handling to their code has improved their effectiveness drastically.

Another topic that had a lot of feedback that kind of links to the AI was the fact that combat was too easy and the AI was not very challenging. Again, I agreed to this. Coupled with the AI improvements, I decided to completely remove instant kill headshots. It is still possible to kill an enemy in a single shot to the head, but you'll need a weapon that deals a lot of damage instead of being able to instant-kill anything you hit with any weapon in the head. Now, the damage done from headshots is changed from instantly depleting enemy health to 0 to now doing the weapon's damage +75 additional damage. Since the standard human npc enemy has 100 health, most weapons will still kill in a single headshot, but may add some extra dynamic combat situations where an extra shot or two is necessary.

A lot of work has gone into improving the way certain entities (objects) act and feel in the game. From simple things such as a tree all the way to advanced things such as buildings have had extensive work to make them act better in the game. Trees have had a lot of work done to make clipping and their physics obstacles be reduced and allow easier and more fluid movement around them. Buildings and many other entities have had material updates, some texture changes, physics improvements, and other sublte but important changes.

More work has gone into brainstorming interesting locations, scenes, and plot material for the storyline. There is a lot of plans and stuff in the process of being made and a lot more content is to come.

Stay tuned, as there will be a lot more news and updates to come!

notes.title: Affliction - 11/5/17 Status Update/Crosshair Poll
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hello there everyone!

Hope you're enjoying the game so far, even in it's current early stages. 

Work continues to improve the game in various ways and I wanted to take the time to talk about some upcoming changes and improvements with the next update.

One thing that I got a lot of feedback about was the HUD system and it's very basic information. For example, the HUD would display "rifle" when holding an AK47/AKM. This was a placeholder for the time. The next update will display actual weapon names for all of the weapons on the HUD, display the correct ammunition type and image.

The AK47 has been renamed to "AKM" as the actual AK47 is no longer in service by any modernized country. The AKM is a modernized version of the AK47 for those of you that do not know.

The Makarov has been renamed to "Makarov PM". The PM literally stands for Pistolet Makarova - Makarov Pistol. Even though it is technically already in the name, this is the proper designation.

All ammunition in the game is now completely technically correct and will display how much you get when picking it up. Changes are displayed below:

Old - New
AK47 Ammo - 7.62x39mm Soviet Rounds
Agram 2000 Ammo - 9x19mm Parabellum Rounds
Makarov Ammo - 9x18mm PM Rounds
Baikal MP 153 Shells - 12x70mm Buckshot Shells
SVD Dragunov Ammo - 7.62x54mm R Rounds

Another major change is the addition of a crosshair. If any crosshair is added, it will be very simple and small. The game is meant to be slightly difficult and slightly more realistic in terms of combat mechanics, so Iron Sights are encouraged to use, but if the community wants a crosshair, it may be added. This may or may not happen depending on the poll which can be taken here: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/K27LFTZ

notes.content:
Affliction,

Hello everyone!

I've been listening to the community over the past few days and hard at work to improve on and fix issues currently present in the game. notes.title: Affliction - 10/13/17 Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Here's another quick status update!

We've finished our self testing and have made several changes as well as additions to the game.

One of our biggest changes regards the physics system. Right now, we've added a very simple system that allows you to pick up and move certain objects around to help with certain sections of the game. For example: you may need to move a box or crate to help you get over something. Objects that can be moved are labeled when you get close enough for easy recognition. In the future, more of these will be added and probably used for simple puzzles. We were quite unsure about how the physics system would handle this but to our surprise, it works very well.

We've fine tuned the "Last Chance" system that I announced a few days ago and we think it works really well now. The conditions have been modified with some special effects so it will really feel like you're fighting for your life.

We've added several more health item pick ups to the game as we felt before that they were too rare.

Ammo was found to be a little too plentiful in some areas, so some of the pick ups for that have been removed or have had their quantity lowered.

We're re-enabled text pop ups when you're near items to help players out by telling them what can be interacted with and what cannot. Note that this is only for item pick ups and weapons. This is not for doors and interaction objects.

We've added more enemies to the game to make it feel like more of a shooter with RPG elements instead of an RPG with shooter elements. That is the way it is intended to be. Think of games such as Cry of Fear, Silent Hill, The Evil Within, Singularity, Dead Space, Resident Evil, Doom, and so on.

The enemy health system has been tweaked for certain enemies so that some are more difficult than others (as intended) and need different tactics to be taken down. Of course, a ton of lead will still do the trick in any case. ;-)

Brightness and contrast in the game has been adjusted to make the game a bit brighter as in our testing we found that the game was a bit too dark. Now, it should be bright enough to see and interact without issue, but still give off the spooky feeling of being alone in the darkness.

Cinematics have had some work done to them as well. Before, they were a little sloppy and rushed but they were merely placeholders for the time being. Now, they are much more atmospheric and carefully done.

I fully expect that within the next few days, the public build will be uploaded to Steam and then after Valve checks it out, it will be released!

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - 10/10/17 Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey everyone, here's another quick status update regarding our progress with the game. ːAflashlightː

I wanted to talk about a new feature that I added today and go over how it works. Something I dubbed the "Last Chance" system. ːAbandagesː

Basically it works like this: When you have 100 health, you'll be given the "Last Chance". It will display on your HUD (Heads Up Display) as a big "1" next to a damaged heart. When you reach 35 health or below, that 1 will change to a "0" and you'll lose the "Last Chance" temporarily, but you'll be given an additional 15 health (may change in the future based on feedback) to give you one last chance - hence the name - to save yourself. Now, the only way to get that "Last Chance" back is to reach 100 health again and fully recover. The player has a natural health regeneration of 1 health every 15 seconds (again, this may also change in the future based on feedback) so it's possible to regain this "Last Chance" without needing to find medical items like medical kits and bandages but it'll take some time. This helps encourage using cover and cutting back on the whole "run n gun" mentality. This game is not meant for that. It is possible you won't always actually get a "Last Chance" because some weapons are more than capable of doing large amounts of damage in an instant. For example, the Dragunov SVD sniper rifle. That is a powerhouse of a weapon and very dangerous. It could (in some cases)  potentially do enough damage to lower you past the point where you'd lose the "Last Chance" and regain some health but still kill you. We're aware of this, and that is how it is meant to be. Enemies and the player do the same amount of damage. There are no handicaps on the NPCs. The player will need to be smart in how they engage enemies and pick their fights wisely. ːArifleː

The addition of this feature also fixes an annoyance (not really a bug but something that didn't completely act the way we wanted) - the lives counter. With the engine that we chose to use, there is a hard coded (unchangable) feature that displays how many lives you have on your HUD. Since the game is realistic, you only have 1 life. So, it reminded you that you always have 1 life only which was pointless. Now, we've combined the lives system with the "Last Chance" system so now you know when you have that reserve "Last Chance" and when you do not. ːAsyringeː

Another thing we've worked on is getting the load times down and we've had great success. We previously had load times of over several minutes in length for a short and simple map, now they take between 10 and 30 seconds only. That is a tenth of our previous load times. We've also been able to increase the quality of the graphics all while still keeping performance good and stable. The game is really starting to take form and be capable of showing the true potential that it has. ːAmagazineː

Let me know what you guys think! We want feedback! ːWWFAKː

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː

Affliction,

So, I have some good news!

Yesterday, I was able to get the AI to be able to completely move without needing player interaction. They can now wander, patrol, hunt, and so on. AI soldiers who see or hear something will now hunt for a semi random amount of time before returning to a calm state and returning to what they were previously doing.

I put some more work into fine tuning the weapons again too. I feel that the changes I made make the weapons have a bit more "impact" in the game. From physics force applied, to damage, to sounds. I'll have some video footage shortly for this. I recently invested in a video creation application that should help out a lot.

I have decided to implement a side healing system along side the health item pickups in the game. As of right now, the player regenerates 1 health every 15 seconds. That may increase but will likely not decrease. The game is meant to be more realistic but I found that the player will almost always have at least some damage and I wanted to add a way to slowly regain lost health. Health pickups will be common, but not to the point where you find one around every corner. Depending on feedback and community opinion, I may completely remove this later. For now, I think it adds a way to help players get along through the game.

The reason I felt it was a good idea to add the healing system is because the game is an action game before anything else. It has several sub-genres but it is an action game. Just health pickups would make some parts extremely difficult and require many attempts. This way, players at least have a chance. I feel it needs balance so people won't abuse it.

I'll continue to keep everyone posted. Please post comments and thoughts on this.

notes.title: Affliction - Sound Overhaul Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey everyone!

I wanted to post another quick status update about the work that I accomplished yesterday.

I finished up the ai code for all of the npcs ai in the game. This doesn't mean they won't be improved on or fixed if there are bugs in the future, it just means that they work well, and they do their job for the time being.

Another thing I took care of yesterday was the player sound effects. Footsteps now sound heavier and they give a real "boots on the ground" feeling. They make the game much more immersive than the old stock ones. I don't want anything stock, I want everything to be unique, so I'm going out of my way to do so. I'm hoping that when players hear the difference, they'll agree with me that they are much better.

Atmospheric sound effects have also been improved so they should give a much better immersive feel.

Within the next few weeks, I plan to do the voice acting and sound effects for the human npcs. I think those will turn out pretty well, as I have voice masking software which can do many different effects.

Weapon sound effects have been taken care of, but they still act a little strange now and then. The way the engine handles automatic fire is quite different so they will still be worked on.

Another thing I did was reduce overall movement speed slightly, and increase the footstep sound rate dramatically. Before I did this, the player moved very fast and footstep sounds were too far apart. Think of a person taking steps of about 5 feet long. Yes, it was bad. Now, they fit directly with the animation and speed of acceleration. To go with this, I also increased the camera wobble when moving but only slightly. I personally dislike games that over dramatize camera sway from movement so I did this very sparingly.

We're getting there, it really shouldn't be too much longer before I have something playable. Technically, I do now, but it isn't much. I need to complete more mapping first before I release anything. I hope you all understand why things are taking this long, I'm really trying to set this apart from the mass of other (mostly sub-par) products from this engine.

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - NPC & AI Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey everyone!

Today I had great success and got a ton of things accomplished. From finishing up the npc models, finishing the ai, almost completing the ai sound effects, to enhancing ai combat behavior and so on.

These were some things that have been on my to-do list for a very long time but now I can comfortably say that everything that has to do with the ai or npcs is almost completed. If I had to give an estimate, I'd say they are 90% fully completed.

As of right now, there are over 25 different human enemy types and over 25 different monsters to fight. They are not just retextured versions either. There are several distinct monster and human enemy "classes".

The stock ai that comes with the engine by default isn't the best, but it is decent, so I have been going through each and every script and changing the code to be much more reactive, smarter, and more challenging. I wanted to make it unique of course as well.

Enemies can react to sounds (not necessarily the player) and sight of course. They can also react to "situational awareness" like sitting behind an enemy while trying to sneak by but taking too long. 

Certain enemies also have a "territory" radius which will cause them to become aggravated if the player enters.

Human ai will use cover, patrol, suppress, and flank in order to create a realistic and challenging combat simulation.

Monster ai will use all sorts of different tactics to kill their prey including charging, sneaking, leaping, and even pretending to be dead in some cases.

One of the major things I wanted to focus on with Affliction was sound effects. Since the graphics are not AAA quality, atmosphere and sound are extremely important in a game like this so I have gone out of my way to purchase and create dozens of sound effects that I feel will really serve the game well. I can't wait to show everyone!

I also finished up the HUD and made it look really good, if I do say so myself. It fits well with the theme of the game. I'll have pictures soon and new videos soon.

The last thing I wanted to mention was optimization. To help with performance and keep the game running smooth, I've made the decision to make slightly smaller maps, but make more of them. This will make it necessary to have more loading screens, but it'll reduce overall loading times, and also help keep a steady fps. I will continue to work on optimization and hope to further improve performance as time goes on.

The game should be ready for Early Access players soon!

As always, please stay tuned for more updates and let me know what you guys think.

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - 6/4/17 Status Update
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hey everyone!

I wanted to stop by and give a status update on the development progress of Affliction.

The first map is nearly completed, it just needs to be populated with items, enemies, etc. It came out looking really well, or so we believe. Over the course of two weeks, the map itself took up over 18 hours to create so far. We put a lot of time and care into the design of our games so we can make as enjoyable of an experience as we possibly can. It may take us longer to finish the game, but we strongly believe it will be worth it in the end.

A large amount of work is already done on the second map, but it is nowhere near completed. We'll have updates on that whenever possible. 

We're planning to have a lot of different maps and scenarios that form a greater story so the mapping will take time.

Weaponry in the game is fairly finished, at the exception of new weapons being added. Currently there are six weapons in the game, but we may be adding a few more.

Enemies in the game already have a lot of variety and there are tons of them, but we're going to continue to explore different ideas and see what fits into the game.

Systems such as the HUD, movement, and interaction are still being fine tuned and will most likely be polished and altered until release.

Sound effects are still something that we'll be working on, probably until release.

Items in the game are also nearly finished. There are several items which can help players on their adventure ranging from bandages to a flashlight. There are also going to be a ton of lore items to help the story move along and give background information as well as useful hints and tips that can help the player in a bind.

The storyline is all thought out and planned but we're still looking into different possibilities about presentation.

The roleplaying version of the game has been revamped and revised several times. We believe it is now in a very fun and enjoyable state. We will release this just as we've released the roleplaying rules for our previous games.

The soundtrack for the game is completed and we think it came out sounding great. We can't wait to see what everyone has to say.

Artwork for the game is done too. We're just working on getting some extras for the storyline.

Anything I've forgotten to mention is likely to be added later or in future status updates. I've requested to put the game into Early Access mode so players can enjoy it early, get a discount for buying it early, and help contribute ideas to making a better game. Like our previous work, we believe the best games are created when the people playing them have a say about how or what the game is. Early buyers will play the game almost as if it were in episodes upon the release of each new update and each major update will feature a new map/mission. That is the plan.

Like always, I'll continue to keep everyone updated.

notes.title: Affliction - Status Update 1/Q&A
notes.content:
Affliction,

Hello everyone, just wanted to stop by real quick and give you a status update.

As many of you know, we've been working on mapping, character design, fighting issues with the engine itself, and we've been working on features for the core of the game. 

What we've accomplished so far this week is that we've added a field of view feature that changes when the player runs/sprints. We've seen this in many games and feel that it really gives the illusion of speed and looks pretty awesome. We hope you'll agree. We didn't make the camera shake like crazy or anything drastic or ridiculous like that, that stuff is just annoying. Another thing we've done this week is we've started on the maintenance sector of the facility and so far it looks pretty awesome. Narrow corridors combined with side rooms for storage and utilities make the maintenance sector an interesting place to venture through. For the time being, we've removed crosshairs from the game and the reason for this is because it made the combat extremely easy. Weapons do have a range system but most of the combat in the game will be medium or close range and the crosshair just made it too easy - no skill or strategy required.

To give everyone who's wondering a little more information about the game, I wanted to answer some questions that I recently was asked.

Q: Are there going to be jumpscares?
A: If there are any, they will be VERY few and far between. Probably not, though.

Q: How much is the game going to be?
A: That hasn't been determined yet, but it will reflect how much content there is in the game. Probably around $9.99.

Q: What enemies do you fight in the game?
A: The game will feature several types of enemies that are split among a few different groups. As of right now, there are four groups. These include the civilians (neutral), the facility security (hostile), the military (hostile), and the afflicted (hostile). Civilians will only be encountered once in a great while unless they are dead. The facility security will be encountered early game and they will put up a decent fight and have some good rewards for taking them down. The military will be a real force to be reckoned with. They will have the very best gear and equipment available in the game. They also have a wide variety of character classes and loadouts that will make each encounter dangerous and require a different approach. The afflicted will be the main enemy in the game. Several variations will be in the game for the afflicted. There will be highly sophisticated and mutated creatures, mutated animals, and weaker and less mutated beings that will act much like zombies. These enemies will not be slow in the game, they will be fast and pose an actual threat.

Q: What is the main objective of the game?
A: Although it may not be entirely clear, you're objective is to escape the facility, fight your way through whoever or whatever stands in your way to freedom and solace, and survive. The game is story driven, but it will be more open world than many story driven games.

Q: What do you mean when you say "no hand holding"?
A: The game will force players to actually think for themselves instead of telling them how to do every little thing and where to go and what to do. It won't be completely directionless and will have a tutorial, but it won't help you with a minimap, tons of health items available, tons of ammo or weapons, etc. We're going to try to give you an enjoyable game that let's you play how you want.

Q: When will it be ready?
A: There isn't an exact date. We plan to have it done by the end of 2017 to the middle of 2018. Yes, it'll take awhile, but take in mind it's only one guy (me) working on the main game and contracting out to others for certain things like music, sound effects, very complex code, and artwork.

Q: Can I participate in development?
A: I always encourage the community to get involved in any way they can. The game is being made for the players, why not have ideas from the players?

Q: Can you fight back in this game?
A: Yes!

Q: What weapons will be in the game?
A: Currently, we have the combat knife, the makarov handgun, the agram 2000 sub machine gun, the mp153 baikal shotgun, the ak47 assault rifle, and the dragunov svd sniper rifle. More may come in the future.

Q: What engine are you using?
A: We're using a program that many of you have probably seen called Game Guru. It's designed for small indie teams and we feel that it is a pretty decent engine. This is our first 3D game so we wanted to start off with something that wasn't too terribly complex.

Q: Can I donate?
A: Yes, you can do so here: https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr?cmd=_donations&business=eplasencia.rvn%40gmail.com&lc=US&item_name=Corrosive%20Studios%20LLC¤cy_code=USD&bn=PP-DonationsBF%3abtn_donateCC_LG.gif%3aNonHosted

I think that just about wraps everything up. If you have other questions, feel free to post them here!

-Corrosion ːCStudiosː
